- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 79.16 → 80+ forecast), then undercorrects.
- Underestimates in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days), suggesting lag or mean-reversion bias.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes, missing volatility spikes.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the 30d forecast, particularly when history includes recent high prices.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5%, model often fails to adjust downward in subsequent days.
- Model underestimates when true outcome shows strong downward momentum after a spike.
- Forecasts show less sensitivity to recent low prices than to recent highs.
